strings.d1.s0.name: Louvre Müzesi
strings.d1.s0.tips: Head straight for the Mona Lisa, then the Denon wing. Book a timed ticket online (32 EUR for non-EU visitors); the Carrousel entrance has no queue.
strings.d1.s1.name: Jardin des Tuileries
strings.d1.s1.tips: Stroll through the gardens from the Louvre to Concorde; look for the green chairs.
strings.d1.s2.name: Café Kitsuné Palais Royal
strings.d1.s2.tips: Coffee and a sandwich in the Palais Royal garden, in a colonnaded courtyard.
strings.d1.s3.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
strings.d1.s3.tips: Monet's Water Lilies in oval rooms; right next to the Louvre and quiet.
strings.d1.s4.name: Eiffel Tower
strings.d1.s4.tips: Take the stairs to the 2nd floor, then the lift to the summit (combined ticket ~29 EUR). Book online and go at sunset; take photos from Trocadéro.
strings.d1.b0.name: Le Petit Cler
strings.d1.b0.tips: A bistro on Rue Cler, close to the Eiffel Tower.
strings.d1.b1.name: Champ de Mars
strings.d1.b1.tips: Lawns beneath the tower; picnic here and watch the light show (every hour on the hour).
strings.d2.theme: Île de la Cité, Latin Quarter and Saint-Germain
strings.d2.s0.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
strings.d2.s0.tips: The restored cathedral is free; reserve a time slot online. Mornings are quiet.
strings.d2.s1.name: Sainte-Chapelle
strings.d2.s1.tips: 1,113 stained-glass panels, at their best on a sunny morning. Book online.
strings.d2.s2.name: Shakespeare and Company
strings.d2.s2.tips: The legendary English-language bookshop on the banks of the Seine.
strings.d2.s3.name: Le Comptoir du Panthéon
strings.d2.s3.tips: A bistro opposite the Panthéon, with steak-frites and a terrace.
strings.d2.s4.name: Panthéon
strings.d2.s4.tips: The tombs of Voltaire, Hugo and Curie; Foucault's pendulum.
strings.d2.b0.name: Bouillon Racine
strings.d2.b0.tips: An Art Nouveau bouillon with an inexpensive classic French menu.
strings.d2.b1.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
strings.d2.b1.tips: The Senate gardens, with a pond and chairs; go here instead of the Panthéon.
strings.d3.s0.name: Sacré-Cœur
strings.d3.s0.tips: The basilica is free; the dome costs 8 EUR. The steps are empty in the morning, with views over Paris.
strings.d3.s1.name: Place du Tertre
strings.d3.s1.tips: The painters' square; portraits cost 40-60 EUR, and you can haggle.
strings.d3.s2.name: Montmartre Vineyard and Lapin Agile
strings.d3.s2.tips: Paris's last vineyard and a cabaret, on Rue des Saules.
strings.d3.s3.name: Chantoiseau Montmartre
strings.d3.s3.tips: A neo-bistro 7 minutes from Place du Tertre, with a set lunch menu.
strings.d3.s4.name: Musée de Montmartre
strings.d3.s4.tips: Renoir's studio and gardens, with views over the vineyard.
strings.d3.b0.name: Boulangerie Pain Pain
strings.d3.b0.tips: Award-winning baguettes and pastries; a quick lunch.
strings.d3.b1.name: Moulin Rouge
strings.d3.b1.tips: See it from outside in Pigalle; the evening show is extra (~120 EUR).
strings.d4.s0.name: Place des Vosges
strings.d4.s0.tips: The oldest square in Paris, with arcades and Victor Hugo's house (free).
strings.d4.s1.name: Musée Picasso Paris
strings.d4.s1.tips: The Picasso collection in the Hôtel Salé. Book online.
strings.d4.s2.name: L'As du Fallafel
strings.d4.s2.tips: The falafel place on Rue des Rosiers with a queue out front; eat standing up.
strings.d4.s3.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
strings.d4.s3.tips: The oldest market in Paris, with Moroccan, Japanese and Lebanese stalls.
strings.d4.s4.name: Centre Pompidou
strings.d4.s4.tips: Inside-out architecture, modern art and views of Paris from the terrace. It is under renovation in 2025-30; if it is closed, go to the Bourse de Commerce.
strings.d4.b0.name: Bourse de Commerce Pinault Collection
strings.d4.b0.tips: Tadao Ando's concrete cylinder and contemporary art; the alternative if the Pompidou is closed.
strings.d4.b1.name: Au Petit Versailles du Marais
strings.d4.b1.tips: Award-winning croissants and quiche; an alternative to the falafel.
strings.d5.s0.name: Musée d'Orsay
strings.d5.s0.tips: Impressionists in a former railway station. Van Gogh is on the 5th floor; photograph the clock face. Book online.
strings.d5.s1.name: Rue du Bac & Le Bon Marché
strings.d5.s1.tips: The Grande Épicerie food hall; good for souvenirs.
strings.d5.s2.name: Café de Flore
strings.d5.s2.tips: Saint-Germain's literary café; try the croque monsieur and hot chocolate.
strings.d5.s3.name: Pont des Arts and the Seine Embankment
strings.d5.s3.tips: See the Île de la Cité from the bridge, then walk along the riverside path.
strings.d5.s4.name: Bateaux Parisiens Seine Cruise
strings.d5.s4.tips: A 1-hour river cruise; Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower in sunset light. Board at the Eiffel Tower pier.
strings.d5.b0.name: Bateaux Mouches
strings.d5.b0.tips: The other cruise company, boarding at Pont de l'Alma.
strings.d5.b1.name: La Grande Épicerie de Paris
strings.d5.b1.tips: The food hall at Le Bon Marché; have lunch at the counters instead of Café de Flore.
strings.d6.s0.name: Palace of Versailles
strings.d6.s0.tips: 45 minutes by RER C. Get the palace, gardens and Trianon passport (~32 EUR); the Hall of Mirrors is empty when it opens at 09:00.
strings.d6.s1.name: Gardens of Versailles
strings.d6.s1.tips: Le Nôtre's gardens; in summer, the musical fountain days (extra ticket).
strings.d6.s2.name: La Flottille Versailles
strings.d6.s2.tips: A restaurant beside the Grand Canal, with rowing boats for hire next door.
strings.d6.s3.name: Petit Trianon and Hameau de la Reine
strings.d6.s3.tips: Marie Antoinette's hamlet and the queen's farm; included with the passport.
strings.d6.s4.name: Marché Notre-Dame Versailles
strings.d6.s4.tips: A food market in town; pick up cheese on your way back.
strings.d6.b0.name: Angelina Versailles
strings.d6.b0.tips: Hot chocolate and Mont-Blanc inside the palace.
strings.d6.b1.name: Grand Trianon
strings.d6.b1.tips: A pink marble pavilion; go here instead of the Petit Trianon.
strings.d7.theme: Canal Saint-Martin and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Canal Saint-Martin
strings.d7.s0.tips: Iron footbridges and canal locks; have a morning coffee and spot the Amélie film locations.
strings.d7.s1.name: Du Pain et des Idées
strings.d7.s1.tips: One of the best bakeries in Paris; try the chocolate-pistachio escargot.
strings.d7.s2.name: Marché d'Aligre
strings.d7.s2.tips: A daily market at Bastille, good for cheese and food souvenirs.
strings.d7.s3.name: Le Baron Rouge
strings.d7.s3.tips: A wine bar next to the Aligre market; oysters and wine from the barrel for a farewell.
strings.d7.s4.name: Gare du Nord / RER B
strings.d7.s4.tips: RER B to CDG takes 35 minutes. Goodbye, Paris.
strings.d7.b0.name: Holybelly Canal
strings.d7.b1.name: Coulée Verte René-Dumont
strings.d7.b1.tips: A green walkway on a former railway line; go here instead of Aligre.
strings.note0: Use a Navigo Easy with a t+ carnet on the metro; take RER C to Versailles and RER B to CDG (11 EUR). The city is walkable: don't take the metro for 20-minute distances.
strings.note1: Timed online tickets are essential for the Louvre, Orsay and Sainte-Chapelle. The Louvre is closed on Tuesdays and Orsay on Mondays. The Paris Museum Pass is available for 2 to 6 days.
strings.note2: Summer brings 25-30°C and daylight until 22:00. Head to the Seine banks (Paris Plages), picnics and terraces. Some bistros close for holiday in August.
strings.note3: A bistro set lunch (formule) costs 18-25 EUR, about half the price of dinner. Tap water (carafe d'eau) is free; for a tip, just round up the bill.
strings.note4: Bouillons (Chartier, Racine) are cheap and classic; go for falafel in the Marais and croissants at Pain Pain or Du Pain et des Idées.
strings.note5: Watch out for pickpockets on metro line 1 and in Montmartre; wear your backpack on your front.
strings.transit.name: Navigo Easy / t+ carnet
strings.transit.why_chosen: Covers metro, RER and buses; a carnet of 10 is the most practical option, with an extra ticket needed for RER C to Versailles.
